messages:
Emma (support): FYI support case #98371 — customer reports gaps in audit exports to their SIEM after they rotated KMS key last week. Missing events include token_create, api_key.rotate, and many embed_request events.
Raj (eng-sre): can you paste the export manifest / S3 path and example missing request_ids?
Emma (support): s3://redwood-audit-exports/acmehealth/2026/03/12/manifest.json
Emma (support): example missing request_ids: abc1234, def5678, ghi9012 — present in internal request logs but not in export files delivered to their Splunk HEC.
Marta (security): did they rotate the KMS key or change the export IAM role around the same time? KMS rotation can alter envelope metadata and the forwarder might reject objects it can't decrypt.
Sofia (acme): we rotated the key on 2026-03-12 02:14 UTC and updated the key ARN in the console at ~02:20. Export was running; we saw a drop starting at 02:25 and it resumed around 03:40.
Leo (infra): pinging export-lambda and siem-forwarder teams. Initial hypothesis: rolling key rotation created a short window where S3 objects are encrypted with a different key id and the forwarder fails decryption and skips them.
Raj (eng-sre): can you share forwarder logs for that window? grep for request_ids or s3 object names.
Leo (infra): log snippet from siem-forwarder (03:24 UTC):
```
2026-03-12T03:24:12Z ERROR forwarder/worker.go:87 failed to fetch s3 object acmehealth/2026/03/12/part-0004.json: s3:GetObject failed: InvalidObjectState: The encryption context doesn't match
2026-03-12T03:24:12Z INFO forwarder/worker.go:112 skipping object acmehealth/2026/03/12/part-0004.json
```
Marta (security): InvalidObjectState indicates a KMS context/key mismatch. Support logs show the audit service did write entries for those request_ids, so the issue is during export/forwarding, not generation.
Emma (support): customer also says schema changed — they expected top-level field "request_type" but in some batches it's nested under "payload.meta.request_type". Could that cause SIEM parsing to miss events even if exported?
Raj (eng-sre): looks like two simultaneous issues: (A) objects skipped due to decryption errors from KMS rotation, (B) a v3 export schema change that wasn't communicated. We'll track both.
Leo (infra): for (A) quick mitigation: forwarder should retry transient KMS errors and write problematic objects to a DLQ bucket for manual reprocessing. Open PR: https://git.internal/repo/siem-forwarder/pull/412 — adds 5 retries with exponential backoff and DLQ write.
Sofia (acme): is there an ETA to re-deliver missing objects? Our SOC needs them for compliance reporting.
Marta (security): we can re-run the export for that time range if infra provides the list of skipped objects. I'll coordinate with legal if retention or privacy review is needed.
Leo (infra): ran a scanner; found 23 skipped objects between 02:25 and 03:45 UTC. Uploaded list to /internal/incident/98371/skipped_objects.txt and attached to the support ticket.
Emma (support): updated ticket #98371 and notified the customer. Next steps: (1) infra to reprocess skipped objects into forwarder DLQ -> push to customer's HEC, (2) eng to merge retry+DLQ hotfix and monitor, (3) product/devex to publish schema v3 change note and provide mapping for payload.meta -> request_type.
Raj (eng-sre): confirm S3 retention: lifecycle deletes after 45 days; March 12 still within window so re-run is OK. If retention had expired we'd need backups/legal.
Leo (infra): re-delivery ETA: will start reprocessing in 30m, expected <2 hours. I'll post job id when started.
Marta (security): for the postmortem capture: console KMS rotation handoff steps, forwarder behavior on encryption header mismatch, and communication plan for schema changes. Add to eng-security backlog.
Sofia (acme): please cc SOC inbox on re-delivery so they can ingest and validate.
Emma (support): cc'd SOC: soc-acme@acmehealth.com on ticket. Will follow up when re-delivery completes.
audit-bot: automated note: export-reprocess job queued id=job-20260312-77, estimated_objects=23, submitted_by=leo
Leo (infra): started job job-20260312-77 at 1755002210
Leo (infra): job finished at 1755003012 status=success forwarded=23
Emma (support): customer confirmed receipt of 23 objects and SOC validated presence of missing request_ids. Closing the support escal.
Marta (security): we'll still publish a short postmortem and the schema mapping note.
Raj (eng-sre): thanks all, marking incident resolved but leaving ticket open for PM/Docs to publish schema compatibility guidance.
